questions.stem: The Haber process uses a temperature of 450°C even though a lower temperature would give a higher yield of ammonia. Why?

options.text: Because the iron catalyst only works at 450°C
Because the equipment cannot withstand lower temperatures
Because 450°C is a compromise: low enough for reasonable yield but high enough for a reasonable rate
Because higher temperatures always give higher yields

questions.explanation: 450°C is a compromise temperature. Since the forward reaction is exothermic, a lower temperature would shift equilibrium to the right, giving a higher yield. However, the rate would be too slow to be economically viable. 450°C provides a reasonable rate while still achieving about 15% conversion per pass.
